mortalidad-oms-colombia.title: Mortality in Colombia, 2000-2023 (WHO)
mortalidad-oms-colombia.notes: Deaths registered in Colombia by year, sex, age group and underlying cause group, taken from the World Health Organization (WHO) Mortality Database and grouped from ICD-10 codes into the same categories as the source files of Colombia, Argentina and Chile. The data are national, with no subnational breakdown.
caveats: This is REFRECA's main mortality dataset for Colombia: its deaths (WHO) and, where incorporated, the United Nations population used as the denominator take precedence over the national source file. That file is kept as a reference in the dataset “Mortality in Colombia, 1985-2020 (Source file: reference)”, which also lets you view the data by department and covers the years 1985-1999.

The data come from the WHO Mortality Database, which only includes the countries and years whose death registration reaches at least 65% coverage; coverage and the quality of cause-of-death certification vary across countries and years.
The series only includes the years with national data coded with ICD-10; earlier years used another revision of the classification.
The WHO also publishes the years 1997, 1998, 1999 with ICD-10; to limit the size of the site, this dataset starts in 2000.
Only deaths whose causes belong to the groups analyzed are kept; all other ICD-10 codes are excluded. Deaths with unknown age appear in the Unknown group.

Quality check: comparing the deaths in the included cause groups according to the WHO with the national source files that REFRECA keeps as reference, the WHO difference from the reference file is: Argentina, 2005-2019: between -1% and 0% per year; Chile, 1997-2019: between -0.3% and +3.9% per year, except 2003, when the reference file is incomplete (1,654 vs. 53,376 deaths); Colombia, 1997-2020: between 0% and +4.4% per year. The differences may be due to later revisions of the records and to cause coding. WHO values are preferred, and so is the United Nations population as the denominator for rates.
The analyses, interpretations and conclusions on this site are those of REFRECA and not of the WHO, which is only responsible for the original information.

Rates use as the denominator the population estimated by the United Nations (World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant, population as of 1 July) for 2000-2023. The deaths come from the WHO Mortality Database, so numerator and denominator have different sources and the rates are approximate.
The United Nations five-year age groups are added up to match those of the dataset (for example, 85+ combines 85-89, 90-94, 95-99 and 100+). Deaths with Unknown sex or age have no population.

consumo-alimentos-2015.title: Food consumption in Colombia, 2015
consumo-alimentos-2015.notes: Percentage of people who report having eaten each of 36 foods or food groups, weighted with the expansion factor, for the national total and by region, area and ethnic group. Calculated from the 2015 food consumption survey (28,902 people); the microdata are not published.
caveats: The consumption frequency variables (Frec_Consumo) use numeric codes from 1 to 10 with no labels in the files received, so they are neither published nor interpreted.
The percentage is calculated over the people who answered Yes or No; blank answers are excluded from the denominator.
The questions on alcoholic and energy drinks have 9,413 blank answers, which are excluded from the denominator.
